content.title: About
content.content: Toasted bread that blends traditional recipes from Italy, Greece and Armenia, offering a crisp crust and a soft, aromatic crumb. The dough is usually made from wheat flour, olive oil, yogurt or kefir, and often flavored with herbs such as oregano, rosemary or cumin, giving it a distinct Mediterranean taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Italian focaccia, Greek pita and Armenian lavash each have unique shapes and thicknesses.
Traditional Armenian bread is baked in a tandoor, imparting a smoky flavor.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a crunchier crust while reducing moisture, extending shelf life.
In the Mediterranean, bread is commonly served with olive oil, feta cheese or hummus.
Ancient Greek myth says bread was a gift from the gods and used in rituals.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Bread provides a steady release of energy thanks to slowly digestible carbohydrates.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions contain dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and folate help metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Bread supplies iron, magnesium and phosphorus, important for blood and bone health.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: When kefir or yogurt is used in the dough, it can promote beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, which can cause issues for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White toasted bread can raise blood sugar quickly, which is undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Salt and fat
items.content: Some recipes use generous amounts of salt or olive oil, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Certain versions may include seeds (sesame, poppy) that trigger allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted bread works well as a base for sandwiches, topped with olive oil, avocado, cheese, ham or vegetables. It can be crumbled into casseroles or served alongside soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bread in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, place it in an airtight container in the refrigerator (up to a week) or freeze (up to 3 months). Warm in the oven before serving to restore a crunchy crust.
